question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)

calls.reasoning: Recent guides were 1.115x-1.145x the quarter just reported, and actuals have beaten the guide midpoint by 4.6-5.7%. So Q3 FY27 should land near $113-114B (analysts project $113-114B), implying a Q4 guide of about $127B. Consensus for Q4 is $124.5B (Yahoo) and the FY consensus implies about $123B, and NVIDIA recently guided about 4% above consensus. Supply limits and the memory-cost squeeze on gross margin pull down; supply agreements jumping to $279B and the 70% FY28 growth outlook pull up. Market check: no human market on the Q4 guide. The Polymarket Q3 Data Center contracts are thin (<$1k volume), internally inconsistent, and measure a different number, so I treated them as weak evidence only.
calls.dossier:
- Q4 FY26 actual revenue ~$68.1B; Q1 FY27 guide $78B (SEC 8-K q4fy26pr; recall-based).
- Q1 FY27 (reported May 20, 2026): revenue $81.6B, Data Center >$75B; Q2 guide $91.0B +/-2%, no China DC compute (NVIDIA PR / stocktitan).
- Q2 FY27 (reported Aug 26, 2026): revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y), Data Center $89.0B; consensus had been $92.27B. Q3 guide $108.0B +/-2% vs consensus $103.9B; GM 74.0% +/-50bp; no China DC compute (coindesk / NVIDIA PR).
- Guide midpoint / prior-quarter actual: 1.145 (Q1), 1.115 (Q2), 1.123 (Q3). Actual vs guide midpoint: Q1 +4.6%, Q2 +5.7%.
- Q3 FY27 consensus: one source says ~$111.4B (chartmill-type aggregators), another ~$109B (search summary), and some analyst projections are $113-114B (cryptobriefing, Seeking Alpha preview).
- Q4 FY27 (Jan 2027 quarter) revenue consensus: average $124.48B, low $117.29B, high $138.49B (Yahoo Finance via search). FY27 consensus is $411.65B, implying Q3+Q4 of about $233.9B.
- Supply agreements: $279B as of Jul 26, 2026, up from $119B a quarter earlier, mostly memory (10-Q via cryptobriefing).
- Management (Aug call): GM expected to bottom at 71-72% in Q4 FY27 on memory cost increases; ~70% FY28 revenue growth, described as supply-constrained (demand would support ~100%).
- Stock lost ~$1.4T in market value over the month before earnings; midterm-election jitters (biggo, Nov 2026).
- Status quo: NVIDIA issues a single midpoint +/-2% in the Outlook section, excluding China DC compute.
- Resolution: resolves off the Q4 FY27 revenue midpoint in the Outlook section of the Q3 FY27 press release (Nov 17, 2026), rounded to the nearest $1B; not the Q3 actual and not Data Center revenue.
- Event window: the Nov 17, 2026 release only; as of Nov 6 the event has not occurred.
- Market check: Polymarket has only Q3 Data Center revenue threshold markets (thin, <$1k volume each, internally inconsistent); no market on the Q4 guide was found.
- Searched but not found: sell-side Q4 guide whispers, any intra-quarter guidance update, and a China license change.

calls.reasoning: NVIDIA's last four next-quarter guides came in $8-12B (12-14.5%) above the prior actual, and each was $13-17B above the previous guide. The Q3 guide was $108B ±2%, and recent beats of $3.6-5.2B imply a Q3 actual around $111-114B, so the Q4 guide lands around $124-129B. Consensus Q4 revenue is about $124.5B, and NVIDIA has guided 4-7% above consensus lately; the 70% FY28 growth forecast and the Rubin/Amazon ramp support upside. Supply/memory limits (margins bottoming at 71-72% in Q4) and no China revenue in the outlook cap it. No human market prices Q4 guidance; the Polymarket contracts on Q3 data-center revenue are thin (volume hundreds), internally inconsistent, and a near-miss contract, so they were not used as an anchor.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same factual base: Q2 actual $96.2B, Q3 guide $108B +/-2%, Q4 consensus ~$124.5B (range $117-138B), and margin trough guidance. The only factual spread is the Q3 consensus/preview range ($109-114B); no web access to settle it, but all sources sit inside the beat-implied band, so it barely moves the median. The rest is judgment about how much the Rubin ramp offsets supply limits. I side with the ratio method and the consensus-plus-premium method, which converge on $127-128B, and keep a modest upside escape for a Rubin-driven step change. I carried Run 3's reference-class framing forward and set the width from the combined uncertainty in the Q3 beat and the guide ratio.
